stem: A nurse is administering an antineoplastic hazardous drug. Which PPE approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Omit PPE when a closed-system drug-transfer device is used because engineering controls eliminate all exposure risk.
options.B: Use a surgical mask alone because room ventilation prevents skin exposure to liquid antineoplastic drugs.
options.C: Use ordinary examination gloves alone because chemotherapy gloves are needed only during drug compounding.
options.D: Wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent protective gown during administration, with additional eye, face, or respiratory protection when the task-specific exposure risk indicates it.

rationale: NIOSH states that during administration or compounding of antineoplastic drugs, healthcare workers should wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent gown with a closed front and tight-fitting cuffs. Engineering controls such as closed-system drug-transfer devices supplement exposure controls rather than eliminate PPE requirements. Additional protection is selected according to the route and likelihood of exposure. D is therefore the best answer; A through C provide inadequate protection.
educational_objective: Use chemotherapy gloves and an appropriate protective gown when administering antineoplastic hazardous drugs, and add task-specific protective equipment when exposure risk warrants it.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
source_document_title: Chemical Hazards Risk Factors — Antineoplastic drugs; Hazardous Drug Exposures in Healthcare
source_version_date: Chemical Hazards page August 12, 2024; NIOSH hazardous-drug resources updated March 3, 2026; accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: Chemical Hazards Risk Factors — Antineoplastic drugs, 'How employers and employees can reduce exposure'; Hazardous Drug Exposures in Healthcare — current resources and control framework
source_claim_supported: During antineoplastic drug administration, NIOSH recommends chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent protective gown; engineering controls reduce but do not eliminate the need for appropriate exposure controls/PPE.

source_original.stem: A nurse administers an antineoplastic hazardous drug. Which PPE approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Omit PPE when a closed-system device is available because engineering controls eliminate all exposure risk
options.B: Use a surgical mask alone because ventilation eliminates skin and mucous-membrane exposure to hazardous drugs
options.C: Use ordinary examination gloves alone because chemotherapy-rated gloves are needed only for drug compounding
options.D: Use chemotherapy gloves and a protective gown, adding eye, face, or respiratory protection as exposure risk requires

source_original.rationale: NIOSH recommends chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent protective gown for antineoplastic drug handling, with additional eye/face or respiratory protection according to the task and exposure risk. Engineering controls supplement rather than automatically eliminate PPE needs.
source_original.source_detail: Healthcare worker controls: chemotherapy gloves, nonabsorbent gown, and task-specific additional controls; Aug. 12, 2024 with 2026 hazardous-drug resources; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Retained the NIOSH-supported PPE construct, verified current 2026 hazardous-drug resources, clarified gown specifications and hierarchy-of-controls wording, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.currentness: NIOSH hazardous-drug hub and antineoplastic-agent resources updated in 2026; core chemical-hazard control page remains current.
audit_findings.claim_audit: NIOSH directly states chemotherapy gloves plus nonabsorbent gown during administration/compounding and describes engineering controls as supplementary controls.

distractor_audit.A: Closed-system devices reduce exposure but do not eliminate all risk/PPE need.
distractor_audit.B: A mask alone does not protect skin from liquid hazardous drugs.
distractor_audit.C: NIOSH calls for chemotherapy gloves during administration as well as compounding.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D provides the baseline PPE directly specified for antineoplastic administration.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are PPE/control strategies; no second defensible combination remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN p.8 explicitly covers hazardous materials and workplace safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read NIOSH antineoplastic controls and 2026 hazardous-drug resources, challenged whether CSTD use could eliminate PPE, and confirmed D remained uniquely correct.
